flawed_step: Proposition 'Strands of 2-ended CAT(0) spaces' (lines 0304-0311), specifically the clause on lines 0309-0310: 'Furthermore sigma is an axis of translation for every hyperbolic isometry of X', together with the proof (lines 0366-0443) which constructs sigma = {c_{Y_0}} x R (line 0405) / {c_{Y_1}} x R (line 0441) out of Min(g^n) for g in Gamma only, and never argues the 'furthermore' clause at all.
counterexample:
Let T be the symmetric tripod: three segments L1, L2, L3, each isometric to [0,1], glued at a common endpoint o; write (i,s) for the point at distance s on leg Li, so d_T((i,s),(j,s')) = s+s' when i != j. Let X = T x R with the product metric: X is a complete proper CAT(0) space (product of a tree and a line) and it is 2-ended. Let phi_12 be the isometry of T swapping L1 and L2 and fixing L3 pointwise, and let Gamma = <gamma> with gamma(y,t) = (phi_12 y, t+1). Gamma is infinite cyclic and acts freely, properly discontinuously and cocompactly on X by isometries (fundamental domain T x [0,1]), so the hypotheses of the Proposition hold exactly.

Run the proof's construction. Gamma is of Z-type, Gamma^+ = Gamma, pi: Gamma -> Z is an isomorphism, so K = ker(pi) = {1}; Aut(K) is trivial, its exponent is n = 1, and g^n = g = gamma. The displacement of gamma at (y,t) is sqrt(d_T(y,phi_12 y)^2 + 1), which equals its minimum 1 exactly on Fix(phi_12) = L3 union {o}. Hence Min(g^n) = Y x R with Y = L3 union {o}, isometric to [0,1]. Gamma acts on Y x R as (identity on Y, t -> t+1), so Gamma' is trivial and Y_0 = Y = [0,1]. Its centre is the midpoint m = (3, 1/2), so the proof outputs the strand sigma = {m} x R.

Now let phi_13 be the isometry of T swapping L1 and L3 and fixing L2 pointwise (legitimate since all legs have length 1), and put gamma' (y,t) = (phi_13 y, t+1), an isometry of X. Its displacement sqrt(d_T(y,phi_13 y)^2 + 1) attains the strictly positive minimum 1 on Fix(phi_13) x R = (L2 union {o}) x R, so gamma' is a hyperbolic (semisimple) isometry of X with translation length |gamma'| = 1 and Min(gamma') = (L2 union {o}) x R; its axes are exactly the lines {y} x R with y in L2 union {o}.

But m = (3,1/2) lies in the interior of L3, and d_T(m, phi_13 m) = d_T((3,1/2),(1,1/2)) = 1/2 + 1/2 = 1, so gamma' displaces every point of sigma by sqrt(1^2 + 1) = sqrt(2) > 1 = |gamma'|. Thus sigma is disjoint from Min(gamma') (indeed gamma' does not even preserve sigma: it maps it to {(1,1/2)} x R), so the constructed Gamma-strand sigma is NOT an axis of the hyperbolic isometry gamma', contradicting the 'furthermore' clause.

The failure is structural, not an artifact: the construction centres only the Gamma-invariant piece Min(g^n) = Y x R, so when Gamma is a proper subgroup of Isom(X) the resulting line is off the Isom(X)-canonical line ({o} x R here) and is only Gamma-canonical. This is exactly the property the later argument uses: the proof of the Assembly Lemma (line 0838) asserts 'the strands in the waffles only depend on the isometry classes of the waffles, so we can pick strand subdivisions for every waffle that is Isom(waffle)-equivariant', and Proposition 'Pattern preserving is close to isometry' (lines 0965-0967) invokes 'the canonicity of strands' to conclude that the combinatorialization carries strands to strands, while the churro-waffle space is built (line 0526) by gluing along strands produced from the smaller group Gamma_churro.
reasoning_summary: Targeted the riskiest concrete assertion, the 'furthermore' clause of the Strands Proposition, which the proof never argues. Built an explicit 2-ended CAT(0) space X = (symmetric tripod) x R with an explicit properly cocompact Z-action gamma = (swap L1,L2 ; t+1). Ran the proof's own recipe: K trivial, n = 1, Min(gamma) = (L3 u {o}) x R, Gamma' trivial, Y_0 = [0,1], centre = midpoint of L3, so the strand is sigma = {(L3,1/2)} x R. The isometry gamma' = (swap L1,L3 ; t+1) is hyperbolic with translation length 1 and Min = (L2 u {o}) x R, while it displaces every point of sigma by sqrt(2). So the constructed Gamma-strand is not an axis of every hyperbolic isometry of X; the construction is canonical only relative to Gamma, whereas the paper later uses strands as data determined by the waffle and its full isometry group (Assembly Lemma proof; 'canonicity of strands' in the combinatorialization-is-close proposition).
